source: All-In Podcast — Anthropic $2T IPO, Zuck's AI manifesto, Nvidia $500B AI financing, Grok 4.6 / SpaceX AI strategy
summary: Anthropic is already profitable/cash-generative; macro bears assuming subsidized tokens are factually wrong
summary_extended: Baker argues that the prevailing macro and value investor assumption that AI tokens are being sold at a loss (i.e., subsidized) is factually incorrect, not merely a difference of opinion. He claims the overwhelming majority of tokens are already profitable for every participant in the inference chain — including Anthropic, OpenAI, and SpaceX AI — and that Anthropic's forthcoming S1 filing will serve as definitive public proof, 'breaking a lot of people's brains' when it confirms profitability. The investment implication is that the bear case built on unsustainable AI economics is structurally flawed, and that frontier AI model companies are viable businesses at current scale, not venture-subsidized loss leaders. Baker frames investors who hold the subsidized-token view as 'ignorant of the facts,' signaling high conviction that this is a mispriced narrative rather than a debatable assumption. No specific revenue figures or margin percentages are cited, but the claim is presented as verifiable via the Anthropic IPO disclosure in the near term.
